title: Desktop Session menu should not cover up button when clicked
line: On the login screen, the Desktop Session menu now opens above its button and marks the selected session.
explanation: The SDDM Breeze theme's SessionButton opened its menu at the button's own top-left corner; since the button sits at the bottom edge of the screen, Qt moved the menu up to fit and it ended up on top of the button. The menu items were plain actions, so nothing showed which session was selected. The menu now opens right above the button, and each item is an exclusive checkable item, so the current session gets a radio mark that follows the choice.

commits.message:
sddm-theme: show the session menu above its button and mark the current one

The desktop session menu popped up over its own button, hiding the control
that opened it, and gave no hint of which session was selected. Open it
above the button instead, and show the selected session with a radio mark.

BUG: 427514

patches.diff:
From 426ca9033e39aae74b628a6c9a2e1e5df63437a6 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Niccol=C3=B2=20Venerandi?= <niccolo@venerandi.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 18:29:23 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] sddm-theme: show the session menu above its button and mark
 the current one

The desktop session menu popped up over its own button, hiding the control
that opened it, and gave no hint of which session was selected. Open it
above the button instead, and show the selected session with a radio mark.

BUG: 427514
---
 sddm-theme/SessionButton.qml | 5 ++++-
 1 file changed, 4 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/sddm-theme/SessionButton.qml b/sddm-theme/SessionButton.qml
index c8ff358362..992545f294 100644
--- a/sddm-theme/SessionButton.qml
+++ b/sddm-theme/SessionButton.qml
@@ -25,7 +25,7 @@ PlasmaComponents.ToolButton {
     checked: menu.opened
     onToggled: {
         if (checked) {
-            menu.popup(root, 0, 0)
+            menu.popup(root, 0, -menu.implicitHeight)
         } else {
             menu.dismiss()
         }
@@ -45,6 +45,9 @@ PlasmaComponents.ToolButton {
             onObjectRemoved: (index, object) => menu.removeItem(object)
             delegate: PlasmaComponents.MenuItem {
                 text: model.name
+                checkable: true
+                autoExclusive: true
+                checked: model.index === root.currentIndex
                 onTriggered: {
                     root.currentIndex = model.index
                     sessionChanged()
-- 
2.53.0

media.caption: Before: clicking "Desktop Session: Plasma (X11)" opens a menu that covers the button, with no mark on the selected session
After: the menu opens above the button, which stays visible, and Plasma (X11) has a radio mark
Before (zoomed): the menu hides the button and doesn't show the current session
After (zoomed): after picking GNOME and reopening, the label and the radio mark both follow the choice

review.text: Addresses both parts of the report cleanly in sddm-theme/SessionButton.qml: opening the menu at -menu.implicitHeight keeps the button visible beneath it, and making the MenuItems checkable with autoExclusive gives the active session a clear radio mark that tracks selection changes. The QML runtime verification and zoomed before/after screenshots confirm the positioning and state updates.

reviews.text: Addresses both parts of the report cleanly in sddm-theme/SessionButton.qml: opening the menu at -menu.implicitHeight keeps the button visible beneath it, and making the MenuItems checkable with autoExclusive gives the active session a clear radio mark that tracks selection changes. The QML runtime verification and zoomed before/after screenshots confirm the positioning and state updates.

The report has two complaints, the menu hiding its own button and no mark for the selected session, and the patch fixes both in the right place (sddm-theme SessionButton.qml): it opens the menu at -implicitHeight above the button and makes the items exclusive checkable items. currentIndex only changes through the menu, so the checked bindings that autoExclusive breaks on click can't fall out of sync. Screenshots show the button staying visible and the radio mark following the choice. The test used a qml harness with stand-in sddm objects instead of a real sddm-greeter, which is acceptable for a QML-only change.
